title: Compromise Authorization Analytics and Evidence Curation Playbook
author: Avery Nguyen
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the detection, containment, and evidence-curation procedures when authorization-related compromise or anomalous entitlement activity is suspected. It covers signals from RBAC/ABAC decision logs, session/authentication traces, audit logging, and data residency considerations necessary for regulatory evidence packaging. Intended audience: security on-call, SRE, platform engineering, and legal/compliance.
body:
1) Purpose and scope
- Purpose: provide a standardized, forensically-sound procedure to detect authorization compromise, contain impact, and curate evidence suitable for internal review and regulatory audit.
- Scope: applies to all Redwood-managed control plane and customer-facing authorization signals (service tokens, user sessions, delegation flows) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Excludes purely application-layer data exfiltration unless tied to authz events.

2) Definitions (quick reference)
- Authorization event: any allow/deny decision emitted by the policy engine (OPA / our in-house gate).
- Entitlement drift: unexpected widening of a principal's effective permissions.
- Authorization telemetry fusion: correlation of decision logs + identity events + request context to produce incident signals.
- Evidence bundle: time-bounded artifact package with immutable audit slices, token snapshots, and custody log.

3) Signals and detection thresholds
- High-confidence signals (immediate pager):
  - >= 10 failed privileged-role activations for a single principal within 5 minutes.
  - Unusual role binding change performed outside business hours (00:00–06:00 UTC) affecting >= 5 entitlements.
  - Deprecated service token used to access customer data plane endpoints.
- Medium-confidence signals (alert to slack/escalation channel):
  - Sudden spike (>200%) in allow decisions for a service identity compared to 7-day baseline.
  - Cross-region session origination not matching recent patterns (new geo + new IP ASN).
- Detection query examples (KQL / SQL-like):
  - Kibana KQL: authorization.decision:deny and event.outcome:failed and timestamp:[now-15m TO now]
  - SQL (audit store): SELECT principal, COUNT(*) as denies_15m FROM authz_decisions WHERE outcome='DENY' AND created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY principal HAVING COUNT(*) > 20;

4) Initial containment checklist (first 30 minutes) — execute in order unless an emergency manual override exists:
1. Triage: capture the alert ID, affected principals, timestamps, and evidence pointer from the detection dashboard.
2. Page on-call security and SRE. Use incident channel #sec-incident and add the incident runbook link.
3. Short-lived session revocation: revoke active sessions for affected principals via the session service API. Example:
   curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_TOKEN" -d '{"principal_id":"user:alice@example.com","reason":"suspected authz compromise"}'
4. Revoke possibly-compromised service tokens by rotating secret scope and issuing stop-order to the token broker. CLI example:
   rwdctl secrets rotate --scope service-xyz --force --comment "revoked due to suspected compromise"
5. Apply temporary authorization guardrail: add deny rule for the affected entitlements at the policy engine with a unique change-id (policy-guard-<INCIDENT_ID>). Record change author and timestamp.
6. Preserve live system state: take API gateway config snapshot, active authz cache dump, and a timestamped export of the policy engine decisions for the 30-minute window.

5) Forensic evidence curation (preservation, indexing, and chain-of-custody)
- Principle: evidence must be immutable, time-bound, and reproducible. Use the Evidence Orchestrator service to capture and sign artifacts. Required artifacts: 
  - Immutable audit slice: authz_decisions and identity events for the incident window (JSON NDJSON), signed with KMS key redwood-evidence-prod.
  - Session manifests: live session table snapshot and active WebSocket/session cookies mapping.
  - Token metadata: token IDs, issuer, scopes, creation and last-used timestamps, and token revocation status. Do NOT include raw secret material in evidence bundles; instead include token IDs and HMAC digests.
  - Gateway access logs (ELB / proxy) and request traces (trace IDs).
  - Policy change history and author metadata.
- Chain-of-custody steps (record as plain text in incident ticket):
  1. Evidence pulled by (operator name), at (timestamp UTC), from (data source).
  2. Evidence packaged into bundle ID: evidence-<INCIDENT_ID>-v1 and signed with KMS key.
  3. Bundle stored in warden-evidence-bucket with object lifecycle: retain 5 years; access controlled by evidence-role.
  4. Access audit: record each read of the bundle in evidence-access-log with approver.

6) Evidence packaging checklist (for auditors)
- Metadata file (metadata.json): incident_id, time_window_start/end, affected_principals, evidence_bundle_id, signer_kms_key, signatures.
- Audit exports (ndjson): authz_decisions.ndjson, identity_events.ndjson.
- Traces: traces.tar.gz (contains per-request trace JSON files).
- Token-index.csv: token_id, service, scope, last_used_ts, revoked_bool.
- Preservation manifest signed and notarized.

7) Retention and data residency mapping
- Governance: evidence bundles for incidents involving customer data must be retained in the customer region when required by contract. Default retention: 5 years for incidents with regulatory scope; 1 year for routine entitlements-only incidents.
- Quick mapping table (text):
  - Incident category: Customer-data-access -> Retention: 5y -> Residency: same-region as data -> Keeper-role: evidence-region-admin
  - Incident category: Entitlement-drift-only -> Retention: 1y -> Residency: US-EU multiregion -> Keeper-role: security-evidence-admin
  - Incident category: False-positive -> Retention: 90d -> Residency: global-log-archive -> Keeper-role: sec-audit

8) Roles and responsibilities
- On-call security (owner): lead triage, call containment steps, request preservation snapshots.
- SRE / Platform (support): run revocation commands, create system snapshots, gather infrastructure-level logs.
- Product / PM (notify): assess customer impact and coordinate customer communications.
- Legal / Compliance (advisor): approve evidence disclosure, advise on cross-border transfer requirements.

9) Post-incident: analysis, regression, and evidence handoff
- Post-incident activities (within 72 hours):
  1. Produce a timeline (mm:ss UTC) of authz events, policy changes, and revocations.
  2. Run authorization telemetry fusion to reconstruct effective access window per principal. Query: authz_fusion.reconstruct(principal, start_ts, end_ts).
  3. Populate the incident evidence index and tag items with compliance labels (SOC2, GDPR, CCPA) as applicable.
  4. Create an RCA (root cause analysis) doc and propose mitigations (policy change, role slimming, JIT requirement).

10) Automation and instrumentation recommendations
- Ship a dedicated detector: "entitlement-drift-detector" with these heuristics: baseline of 7-day moving average, Z-score threshold 4 for role activations, geo anomaly detection using MaxMind ASN tagging.
- Instrument decision logs with these fields: timestamp_utc, principal_id, principal_type, decision_id, outcome, policy_id, rule_id, resource, action, request_id, trace_id, source_region, client_ip_asn, user_agent, decision_latency_ms.
- Store a copy of authz_decisions in an immutable append-only store partitioned by day for at least 365 days.

11) Communication templates
- Internal incident opening message (Slack):
  "[INCIDENT <ID>] Suspected authorization compromise. Affected principals: <list>. On-call: <name>. Action: sessions revoked; policy guard applied; evidence collection in progress. See <link-to-incident-runbook>."
- Customer notification guideline: consult Legal; use pre-approved wording: do not disclose internal mitigations or token details.

12) KPIs and runbook health checks
- Mean time to containment (MTC): target < 30 minutes for high-confidence authz compromise alerts.
- Evidence readiness SLA: evidence bundle assembled and signed within 4 hours of containment.
- Runbook drills: quarterly tabletop exercising for cross-region authorization incidents.

13) Appendices
A. Sample KMS command to sign evidence manifest (internal):
  gcloud kms keys versions sign --location=global --keyring=redwood-evidence --key=evidence-prod --data-file=metadata.json --signature-file=metadata.sig

B. Quick revocation playbook (CLI snippets):
  # revoke a user session
  curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_TOKEN" -d '{"principal_id":"user:alice@example.com"}'

  # add a blocking policy rule in OPA via gitops (ensure PR recorded)
  git checkout -b emergency/deny-guard-<INCIDENT_ID> && echo '{"deny": "true"}' > policies/guard-<INCIDENT_ID>.rego && git commit && git push && open-pr-to-main

C. Evidence handoff template (to Legal)
  - Incident ID:
  - Summary:
  - Bundle ID:
  - Retention recommendation:
  - Cross-border transfer needs:
  - Attachments: metadata.json, authz_decisions.ndjson, token-index.csv

References and related runbooks:
